questions.question: Where were the first Winter Paralympics Games held?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Sweden.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **__Important Points__**

__
 
• The first Winter Paralympics Games were held in Sweden in **1976**.
 
• In these games, athletes with physical disabilities (mobility disabilities, amputations, blindness and cerebral palsy) participate.
 
• **53 athletes from 16 nations** participated in 1976.
 
• These are held after every 4 years.
 
• Organized and managed by **International Paralympic Committee.**
 
• These games are directly preceded by Winter Olympic Games.
 
• **Classification of Paralympic Games –**
 
 
• Alpine Skiing: 2 events – Slalom and Giant Slalom
 
• Biathlon: Combination of cross-country skiing with target shooting
 
• Cross-country Skiing: (known as Nordic Skiing) have 15 classifications
 
• Ice Sledge Hockey: only for males
 
• Wheelchair Curling: coed team event and need a wheelchair for mobility
 
• Para-snowboarding: introduced in 2012
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Russia**: 11th edition in 2014 (opened by President Vladimir Putin)
 
• **Italy**: 9th edition in 2006 (opened by President Carlo Azegilo Ciampi), 14th edition in 2026 (upcoming)
 
• **Korea**: 12th edition in 2018 (opened by President Moon Jae-in)
 
• Current President of South Korea: Yoon Suk-yeol (2022)

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ea728f908b060e4db8cdc0f37188bd8bacc49aff99cc89b07517095538ec56de.png] 

 
• The 13th edition will be held in **Beijing China** in March 2022.
 
• In the 1976 edition, there were only 2 sports i.e. Alpine Skiing and Cross-country skiing.

**1976 Winter Paralympics Games logo held in Sweden**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/00df6b991809a4f3af681fbf4bc4e2f8983b11369e6f56a99bc95a6426a9e3ec.png]

questions.question: In the field of computing, what does VRML stand for?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Virtual Reality Mark Up Language.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• **VRML stands for Virtual Reality Mark Up Language.​**
 
• It is initials, originally known as the **Virtual Reality Markup Language before 1995.**
 
• It is a standard 3-dimensional (3D) interactive vector graphics representation file format, designed especially with the World Wide Web in mind.
 
• VRML is a text file format where, for example, it is possible to specify vertices and edges for a 3D polygon along with the surface color, UV-mapped textures, shininess, transparency, etc.
 
• URLs can be associated with graphical components so that when the user clicks on a specific graphical component, a web browser can pick up a web page or a new VRML file from the Internet.
 
• The user may interact with animations, sounds, lighting, and other aspects of the virtual world or they may be triggered by external events such as timers.
 
• A special Script Node enables the program code (e.g. written in Java or ECMAScript) to be added to a VRML file.
 
• VRML files are commonly referred to as "**worlds**" and have the extension **.wrl** (for example, island. wrl).
 
• VRML files are in plain text and usually compress well using **gzip.**
 
 
• It is useful for faster transfers over the Internet (some gzip compressed files use the .wrz extension).
 
 
 
• Many 3D modeling programs can save objects and scenes in VRML format.

**Apartment Ground Plan in VRML**

questions.concept: India under East India Company’s Rule
questions.question: When did Shuja-ud-daulah and Shah Alam sign treaties at Allahabad with Robert Clive?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**1765.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **__Important Points__**

__
 
• **Treaty of Allahabad** was signed in **1765 **by **Shuja-ud-Daulah and Shah Alam II **with **Robert Clive** marking the beginning of British Rule in India.
 
• Through this treaty, East India Company was granted to collect taxes from the eastern province of** Bengal-Bihar-Orrisa **in return for which Shah Alam II was given Kora and Allahabad.
 
• The company promised to support** Shuja-ud-Daulah, Nawab of Awadh **against attacks which made him dependent on the company for which he had paid **Rs. 53 lakhs.**
 
• This treaty followed the** Battle of Buxar** in which Mughal emperors were lost to the Company.
 
• This treaty made the company richer and now they didn’t require any money from England.
 
• Treaty of Allahabad was written by **I’tisam-ud-Din** who was a diplomat to the Mughal Empire.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Treaties signed in 1766**: Treaty of Batticaloa (Dutch Imperial possession in Sri Lanka)

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ea728f908b060e4db8cdc0f37188bd8bacc49aff99cc89b07517095538ec56de.png] 

 
• Nawab of Bengal was having only judicial powers but the power to collect revenue and taxed was vested in the company.

questions.question: What is the radius of the moon?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**1.74 x 10⁶ m.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **__Important Points__**

__
 
• The radius of the moon is **1737.1 km or 1.74 × 10⁶ m.**
 
• Moon is the only natural satellite of Earth.
 
• Moon is the **5th largest **satellite in the Solar System.
 
• Moon’s age is believed to be **4.53 billion years.**
 
• Moon is **2,38,855 miles **away from the earth.
 
• The gravitational influence of the Moon produces tides on Earth and lengthens the Earth’s day.
 
• Other Points about Moon –
 
 
• Planetary mass object and differentiated rocky body
 
• Lacks atmosphere, hydrosphere, and magnetic field
 
• Sidereal period: 27.3 days and Synodic period: 29.5 days
 
• The lunar surface is non-reflective
 
• Components of Lunar surface: Silica, Alumina, Lime, Iron Oxide, Magnesia, Titanium dioxide, Sodium oxide
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• 1st manmade object to reach the moon: Luna 2 spacecraft (crewless) in 1959 by the Soviet Union
 
• 1st successful soft landing: Luna 9 in 1966
 
• 1st manned mission: Apollo 8 in 1968

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ea728f908b060e4db8cdc0f37188bd8bacc49aff99cc89b07517095538ec56de.png] 

 
• Lunar Eclipse: (Full moon) Earth is between Sun and Moon
 
• Solar Eclipse: (New moon) Moon is between Earth and Sun

**Tinted reddish moon during the lunar eclipse**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/01641ccf9357c4f6124855c82a3e77a8077f15479a2ed96b89b30fe69b7c8aee.png]

questions.question: The mixed economy is:

options.text: co-existence of traditional and modern industries
presence of domestic and foreign investments
a market system of resource allocation, commerce, and trade in which free markets coexist with government intervention
presence of subsistence and commercial farming

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**a market system of resource allocation, commerce, and trade in which free markets coexist with government intervention.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• In a socialist society the government decides what goods are to be produced in accordance with society's needs.
 
• In a **mixed economy**, the market will supply whatever goods and services it can produce well, and the government will provide essential goods and services that the market fails to do. 
 
• The mixed economic system is described as an economic system which combines the elements of a **planned economy** with those of a **market economy. **
 
• It is a mixture of capitalism and socialism, comprising both private and public corporations.
 
• A mixed economy structure is adopted by most developed economies.
 
• The elements of a capitalist economy and the elements of a command economy are synthesized into a mixed economic structure.
 
• Free economies co-exist with government interference in a mixed economic environment, and private businesses coexist with public enterprises.
 
• The benefits of a mixed economy include efficient production and capital distribution, as well as social security development.

**Flowchart showing Mixed Economy Model**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/8c29811ebb74190044f35ce13f6f40579a007b3411df53c2cf96e893ac0a0190.png]

questions.question: Which woman astronaut has set the record for the longest single spaceflight by a woman?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is__** Christina Koch.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **__Important Points__**

__
 
• The longest-ever single spaceflight by a woman was accomplished by NASA** astronaut Christina Koch.**
 
• At about **09:12 GMT**, the **Russian Soyuz **spacecraft carrying Koch parachuted down to the grasslands of Kazakhstan. 
 
• She spent **328 days** on the International Space Station (ISS), surpassing the previous record set by fellow** American Peggy Whitson.**
 
• Her stay is only **12 days** shy of **Scott Kelly,** who was on the ISS from 2015-2016, setting the all-time US record.
 
• On** 28 December 2019**, Ms. Koch exceeded the **289-day** mark held by fellow American Ms. Whitson.
 
• Yet her return to Earth is setting the marker to beat for future space explorers.
 
• Koch accomplished** 5,248 orbits** of the Earth during her mission and traveled** 223 million km (139 million miles)** - the equivalent of 291 round trips from Earth to the Moon.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Peggy Whitson** currently holds the record for a woman's most time spent in space, recorded over the span of three 2002-2017 spaceflights.

**A file photo of Christina Koch**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/37dc8929aa38d7f9a7dc66244bfee88ac2f6dceeb18bd3fcbad5da350e6b526e.png]

questions.question: India is divided into how many earthquake zones (seismic zones)?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is__** 4.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **__Important Points__**

 
• Based on historical seismic activity, the **Bureau of Indian Standards **has categorized regions in India into **four seismic zones: zones II, III, IV and V. **
 
• Of these, the most seismically active area is** Zone V** and the least active is** Zone II. **
 
• There is a history of devastating earthquakes on the Indian subcontinent.
 
• The key cause for the high frequency and severity of earthquakes is that the Indian plate is driving into Asia at a rate of roughly **47 mm/year. **
 
• India's geological figures indicate that about **54 percent** of the land is prone to earthquakes.
 
• Research by the World Bank and the United Nations

questions.question: How many Grand Slam tournaments are played in a year in tennis?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**4.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **__Important Points__**

 
• The four annual tennis tournaments, also known as **majors**, are collectively called the **Grand Slam. **
 
• The** ITF—the International Tennis Federation—**operates the Grand Slam.
 
• The Grand Slam tournaments consist of the **mid-January Australian Open, the late May French Open or Roland Garros, the Wimbledon at the end of June and the US Open at the end of August.**
 
• The **four Grand Slam tennis tournaments** are played over the course of** 2 weeks. **
 
• The oldest is **Wimbledon Tennis, established in 1877,** then comes the **US Open in 1881 followed by the French Open in 1891, and the last is Australian Open in 1905.**
 
• The Australian tennis and US tournaments are played on hard courts,** the French Open on clay courts, and the Wimbledon on grass courts.**
 
• Before 1924-1925, the** French Open tournament** was not considered a Grand Slam.
 
• Together, the four majors are considered a "**boxed set**" of Grand Slam tournaments in all three disciplines (singles, doubles, and mixed doubles).
 
• During the course of a lifetime, winning all four majors is considered a** career Grand Slam.**
 
• It is considered a **non-calendar year Grand Slam** to win the four majors in consecutive events, but not in the same year.

questions.question: Which technology do third generation computers use?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is__** Integrated Circuits.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The third-generation period in computing was from **1965-1971. **
 
• **Integrated circuits (ICs)** have been used in** third-generation computers** instead of transistors.
 
• Along with the related circuitry, a single IC has multiple transistors, resistors, and capacitors.
 
• An American electrical engineer named **Jack Kilby** invented the IC.
 
• This advancement has enhanced the compactness, reliability, and performance of computers. 
 
• **Remote processing, time-sharing and multiprogramming operating systems have been used in this generation.**
 
• During that generation, high-level languages (**FORTRAN-II TO IV, COBOL, PASCAL PL/1, BASIC, ALGOL-68, etc.) **were also used.
 
• **The main features of third-generation are −**
 
 
• IC used
 
• More reliable in comparison to previous two generations
 
• Smaller size
 
• Generated less heat
 
• Faster
 
• Lesser maintenance
 
• Costly
 
• AC required
 
• Consumed lesser electricity
 
• Supported high-level language
 
 
 
• **Some computers of this generation were −**
 
 
• IBM-360 series
 
• Honeywell-6000 series
 
• PDP (Personal Data Processor)
 
• IBM-370/168
 
• TDC-316
 
 

**A Third Generation Computer**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/753b11129d27b293ac44332d371f7c21c37628449bb40596cfb6dd4c5ccee357.png]

questions.question: Animals of which phylum have jointed legs?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Arthropoda.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Arthropoda** is a group of invertebrate animals having an exoskeleton, a segmented body and jointed legs.
 
• Their body consists of segments with a pair of appendages.
 
• Their reproduction occurs by internal fertilization (terrestrial species) and internal or external fertilization (aquatic species).
 
• They have an open circulatory system.
 
• Types of Arthropods –
 
 
• Insects: Ants, Aphids, Butterflies, Grasshoppers, Termites, and etc.
 
• Arachnids: Scorpion, Mites, Spiders
 
• Crustacean: Crabs, Fish, Lobsters, Shrimp, and etc.
 
 
 
• Their evolution dates back to the Cambrian period.
 
• They are a source of food for humans.
 
• They are pollinators of crops.
 
• Some species spread diseases to humans, livestock, and crops.
 
• Largest phylum of invertebrate animals.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Mollusca** – 2nd largest phylum of invertebrate animals mostly found in marine and freshwater having the soft body divided into head, visceral mass, muscular foot, and mantle. Examples: Snail, Octopus, Squid, Oyster, Clams, and etc.
 
• **Nematoda:** bilaterally symmetrical, elongate and tapered at both ends; an important role in nutrient recycling in the soil feed. They cause diseases such as Ascariasis, Enterobiasis, Filariasis, and etc. Examples: Ascarids, Worms
 
• **Echinodermata:** marine animals having a star-like appearance, Echinoderms (Phylum Echinodermata) are a diverse, exclusively marine group of invertebrates.
 
 
• Examples: Starfish, Sea urchins, Crinoids, etc.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/fa1a55bb54b9cadef590bd50eb3bd64b2a36de8895342e9c1eff2382db946414.png] 

 
• All arthropods lay eggs except Scorpion who directly give birth to young.

**Popular species of Arthropods** 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ed3b6b1c4b99539eec0d1f6d5e9c01f6e07ff8b55a8ec9c708864e415ae8b5b5.png]

questions.question: Who was the first Chief Election Commissioner of India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is__** Sukumar Sen.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **__Important Points__**

__
 
• Indian Civil Servant, Sukumar Sen was the first Chief Election Commissioner of India who oversaw India’s general election in **1951-52 and 1957.**
 
• He was succeeded by **Kalyan Sundaram**.
 
• He was also the 1st Chief Election Commissioner in Sudan.
 
• He was 1st Vice-Chancellor of the University of **Burdwan**.
 
• He was awarded **Padma Bhushan**.
 
• **Election Commission of India:**
 
 
• Formed: **25 January 1950.**
 
• Objective: Election to the offices of President, Vice President, Parliament, Legislative Assemblies and Councils.
 
• Operates under **Article 324.**
 
• Removal of Chief Election Commissioner –** By a resolution passed by parliament (the two-third majority in Lok Sabha and Rajya Sabha).**
 
• Removal of Election Commissioner – By President of India on the recommendation of Chief Election Commissioner.
 
• **Article 324 – Article 329:** Related to the Election Commission of India.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Om Prakash Rawat**: 1977 batch IAS officer of Madhya Pradesh, served as 22ⁿd Chief Election Commissioner of India
 
• **Kalyan Sundaram**: 1st Law Secretary of Independent India, served as 2ⁿd Chief Election Commissioner of India, chaired 5th Law Commission of India
 
• **Mihir Sen**: 1st Indian to swim the English Channel (Dover to Calais); the only man to swim Palk Strait, Dardanelles, Bosphorus, Gibraltar, and Panama Canal in one calendar year; World’s greatest long-distance swimmer – Guinness Book of Records

questions.question: Velds are grasslands of:

__
 
• Veldts are grasslands of **Southern Africa **(South Africa, Lesotho, Eswatini, Zimbabwe, and Botswana).
 
• Veldts are covered with grass or low shrub.
 
• On the basis of elevation classified as **High Veld, Middle Veld, and Low Veld.**
 
• Climate: Mild winter (May – September), Hot Summer (November – March), Coldest month (July).
 
• Rainfall: Average annual rainfall is between **15 – 30 inches.**
 
• Support a variety of natural vegetation, Red grass in bush veldts and Acacia and Marula in high veldts.
 
• Surrounded by Drakensberg mountain on the east.
 
• **Main crops**: Maize, Barley, Potatoes, Oats.
 
• Rich reserves of minerals.
 
• **Grasslands –**
 
 
• The area where vegetation is dominated by grass cover.
 
• Naturally occurring in all continents except Antarctica.
 
• Largest biomass on earth and dominate the landscape (31% - 34% area of the earth).
 
• Types: Natural, Semi-natural, Agricultural.

questions.question: The period of second five year plan in India was:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**1956-61.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **__Important Points__**

__
 
• The **Second Five Year Plan** in India was planned under the leadership of **Jawaharlal Nehru** for the period from **1956 to 1961.**
 
• It was based on the** P.C. Mahalanobis **model built-in** 1953.**
 
• Its main emphasis was on the country's economic growth.
 
• This plan lagged below its **4.5 percent** target growth rate and reached a **4.27 percent** growth rate. 
 
• This plan was opposed by many experts, and India faced a payment crisis in **1957 **as a result.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• In India, the** first five-year plan** was initiated in **1951** and India has witnessed **twelve **Five Year Plans since then.
 
• However, the existing government scrapped the Five-Year plan system and a new mechanism was placed in motion.

**Drafting of the Second Five Year Plan**

• In December 2019, China launched the third **Long March-5,** the country's largest carrier rocket, from the **Wenchang Space Launch Centre in southern China's Hainan Province. **
 
• At **8:45 pm (Beijing time**), the rocket, coded as **Long March-5 Y3**, blasted off from the coastal launch centre carrying the **Shijian-20** science experiment satellite weighing over eight tons, the nation's heaviest and most advanced communications satellite.
 
• The satellite was sent into its targeted orbit about **2,220** seconds later.
 
• The Long March-5 is a massive two-stage rocket capable of carrying a payload of **25 tons,** equal to the weight of 16 cars, to low Earth orbit, 14 tons at geostationary orbit, eight tons at Earth-Moon orbit, or five tons at Earth-Mars orbit, more than twice the capacity of the existing main Long March series rockets.
 
• According to the China Aerospace Science and Technology Corporation, the rocket is capable of sending probes to explore Jupiter and other planets in the solar system in tandem with an upper stage (CASC).
 
• The rocket is about **57 meters** in length, equal to a 20-story building's height, with a core stage 5 meters in diameter and four boosters 3.35 meters in diameter.
 
• The Long March-5 is much larger than the previous carrier rockets of China.
 
• It has a takeoff weight of around **870 tons** and a thrust of about 1,000 tons.

questions.question: Who acts as the President during casual vacancy that arises due to death of the President?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is__** Vice President.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• After the President, the Vice President of India is the second-highest constitutional office in India.
 
• **Article 63** of the Indian Constitution specifies that "**There shall be a Vice President of India."**
 
• In the absence of the President due to** illness, retirement, impeachment or other conditions**, the Vice President serves as President.
 
• The Vice President of India is also the **ex officio Chairperson of the Rajya Sabha.**
 
• When a bill is introduced in Rajya Sabha, the vice president decides whether or not it is a financial bill.
 
• If in his view, a bill introduced in the Rajya Sabha is a money bill, he would refer the case for a decision to the Speaker of the Lok Sabha.
 
• **Article 66** of the Indian Constitution lays down the way in which the Vice President is chosen.
 
• The Vice-President shall be chosen indirectly, by means of a single transferable vote, by members of an electoral college composed of members of both Houses of Parliament, in accordance with the system of proportional representation, and shall be elected by secret ballot by an electoral council.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The current Vice President of India is Jagdeep Dhankar**. **

questions.question: Who has won DSC Prize for South Asian Literature 2019?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Amitabha Bagchi.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **__Important Points__**

 
• The novel **Half The Night Is Gone **by Amitabha Bagchi has won **2019 $25,000 DSC Prize **for South Asian Literature, topping a shortlist of six works of fiction.
 
• The winner was announced at the **IME Nepal Literature Festival in Pokhara, Nepal**, where the winner's trophy was presented to Bagchi by **Pradeep Gyawali, Nepal's foreign minister. **
 
• His novel, a post-colonial saga that unfolds over three generations, explores human relationships and the interconnection of fates and cultures in a thoroughly Indian context while paying close attention to detail and the inventive use of language.
 
• His debt to more than one modern Hindi writer is acknowledged by Bagchi himself.

**Amitabha Bagchi receiving the DSC Prize for South Asian Literature 2019**
